item.title: From 10 players to champions
item.description: RATU Nauvula College may have been the lone western school at the Vodafone Super Deans Championship finals, but its under-14 side ensured the West would not leave the HFC Bank National Stadium empty-handed last Saturday. item.content:encoded:
RATU Nauvula College may have been the lone western school at the Vodafone Super Deans Championship finals, but its under-14 side ensured the West would not leave the HFC Bank National Stadium empty-handed last Saturday.

The young Nauvula warriors produced one of the most inspiring stories of the finals, overcoming Queen Victoria School 22-17 to claim the U14 title and carry the hopes of the Western Division with them.

For head coach Viliame Vuetaki, the triumph was the reward for a journey built on faith, hard work and perseverance.

“To be frankly honest, we started training in week one during round one of the competition and, like I said in the semi-finals, we only had two reserves,” Vuetaki said.

“It was only through the Lord that we were able to achieve this.”

The coach’s words reflected the remarkable determination within a team that had entered the competition with modest expectations.

Captain Vero Naovuka revealed that when the team first came together, there were only 10 players.

“When we started the team there were only 10 players. We didn’t expect to come this far, but we just prepared well, trained hard and listened to our coaches,” Naovuka said.

That belief was tested in the closing stages of the final.

With Nauvula holding a slender 22-17 lead inside the final five minutes, Naovuka said the message from the coaching bench was simple — remain calm and defend.

“I told the boys just keep defending and stay composed. When they lose the ball, it will be ours,” he recalled.

They defended their line, absorbed the pressure and refused to surrender the advantage that had taken months of sacrifice to build.

For Vuetaki, however, the victory belonged to more than just the team. He dedicated the achievement to Ratu Nauvula College, the vanua that had stood behind the team throughout its campaign and the parents who supported their children.

But the coach was quick to redirect the spotlight.

“The spotlight belongs to the players and the man above,” he said.

And fittingly, it was the players who wrote the final chapter.

From a team that started with just 10 players to a Deans championship-winning side, Nauvula’s U14 journey was a reminder that in schoolboy rugby, champions are not always built from numbers or reputation.

Sometimes they are built from belief, discipline, sacrifice and the courage to keep going.

On a day when the West stood alone among the finalists, Ratu Nauvula College stood tall.

The West had its champion — and it was a team that simply refused to give up.

item.title: Nasoko franchise – A new beginning for schools rugby in Fiji
item.description: FOR generations, the final whistle of the Deans competition has signalled the end of the secondary schools rugby season. This week, however, that final whistle will signal something entirely different — the beginning of a new pathway.
item.content:encoded:
FOR generations, the final whistle of the Deans competition has signalled the end of the secondary schools rugby season.

This week, however, that final whistle will signal something entirely different — the beginning of a new pathway.

Fiji’s best young rugby players will come together under one banner when the inaugural Nasoko Franchise competition gets underway, bringing the cream of the Vodafone Super Deans and Raluve competitions into a unique national talent identification and development programme.

The initiative will unite the best under-16 and U18 boys and girls from the Eastern, Northern, Southern and Western zones for a week of rugby, assessment, education and development.

But the importance of Nasoko extends far beyond finding out which zone has the strongest team.

Fiji Rugby Union acting chief operations officer Talemo Waqa says that is not the purpose.

“The whole purpose there is for the cream of every zone to come and play together — east versus north, south versus west and so on,” Waqa said.

The teams will play a three-day round-robin competition from Tuesday to Thursday, giving coaches and selectors an opportunity to assess the country’s outstanding young talent.

Friday will then provide another dimension, with the players selected into new combinations for further matches.

“It is not there for whoever has won,” Waqa said.

“No, it’s there to put together formidable U16 and U18 teams, girls and boys.”

For the first time, Fiji Rugby is attempting to bring the best young talent from every corner of the country together immediately after the major secondary schools competitions.

The programme has been put together through the Ministry of Education, Fiji Rugby and the Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union, creating what could become the annual culmination of the schools rugby calendar.

“It has never been done in the past,” Waqa said.

“It is something that we believe is the way forward each year, so that we culminate in such a Nasoko competition.”

That vision could prove significant for the future of the sport.

For too long, the end of a schools competition has often meant the end of meaningful competition for many promising players.

Nasoko is designed to close that gap, allowing Fiji Rugby to immediately identify, assess and begin developing the country’s next generation.

It is also a programme built around more than players.

Coaches, managers, strength and conditioning personnel and match officials will all be part of the development environment, making Nasoko a complete rugby development exercise rather than simply another tournament.

The girls will be based at Namaka Public School, while the boys’ competition will be held in at Ba Provincial High School.

item.title: Rewa show fighting spirit
item.description: THE FMF Rewa Women’s Rugby team may have suffered another defeat 51-30 against Khelvin Civil Engineering Lautoka Women’s in the Subrails Marama Cup Championship, but their round four encounter provided a much-needed boost as the side finally found its way onto the scoreboard at Churchill Park in Lautoka last Saturday. Team manager Frances Qounadovu said the players gave their all throughout the co
item.content:encoded:
THE FMF Rewa Women’s Rugby team may have suffered another defeat 51-30 against Khelvin Civil Engineering Lautoka Women’s in the Subrails Marama Cup Championship, but their round four encounter provided a much-needed boost as the side finally found its way onto the scoreboard at Churchill Park in Lautoka last Saturday.

Team manager Frances Qounadovu said the players gave their all throughout the contest and welcomed the opportunity to compete again after three scoreless matches against Naitasiri, Malolo and Kadavu.

“It was a fair game, we loved every minute of it, the girls gave their all,” Qounadovu said.

After three consecutive games without points, getting on the scoreboard was an important achievement for a Rewa side that has endured a difficult opening to the competition.

The manager credited the players for their determination and thanked God for giving the team strength and the opportunity to experience the game again.

However, the manager acknowledged that there is still considerable work ahead, particularly in fitness, communication and technical skills.

The Rewa Women’s team has also faced challenges beyond the playing field, including limited technical assistance and the need for greater support for the players’ overall well-being.

Despite those difficulties, the team continues to represent young women from Serua, Ovalau and Rewa, bringing together players from different walks of life.

Frances thanked the various clubs within the Rewa Rugby Union, as well as the families who continue to support the players.

As the competition enters its fourth week, she appealed to the public to rally behind women’s rugby.

“One concern highlighted was the small crowd at the Marama Cup match, so I am urging supporters and the public to attend women matches and encourage their women’s team.

“Whatever the result, the Rewa Women’s Team is still there and are still fighting for this season,” Frances said.

The focus now turns to continued improvement and building on the positives from Round Four and more work on the fundamentals.

The Rewa Women’s team remains hopeful of better results as the Marama Cup Championship continues.

They will face Suva Women for Round 5 at the HFC Bank Stadium next weekend.

item.title: Daurua hooks Grammar to Deans glory
item.description: SUVA Grammar School hooker Viliame Daurua produced a powerful performance in the No. 2 jersey, scoring a hat-trick to help end the school’s 21-year wait for Vodafone Super Deans under-18 glory. The Kadavu-born front-rower was a dominant figure as Grammar overwhelmed Lelean Memorial School 36-21 in the finals at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
SUVA Grammar School hooker Viliame Daurua produced a powerful performance in the No. 2 jersey, scoring a hat-trick to help end the school’s 21-year wait for Vodafone Super Deans under-18 glory.

The Kadavu-born front-rower was a dominant figure as Grammar overwhelmed Lelean Memorial School 36-21 in the finals at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on Saturday.

Daurua’s impact was felt from the opening exchanges as Grammar’s powerful forward pack laid the platform for victory.

After Avanua Tevita opened the scoring in the fourth minute, Daurua barged over for his first try before crossing again to complete a double and help Grammar establish a 19-7 halftime lead.

Lelean fought back strongly after the break, closing the gap to 19-14, but Daurua once again answered the challenge.

He crossed for his third try to complete his hat-trick and restore Grammar’s momentum before captain Waisale Bolakoro and Saula Koroi added further tries.

Daurua’s three-try performance earned him the Best Player award, capping a memorable campaign for the young hooker.

“First of all, I want to give thanks to the Almighty for giving me the strength, the strides and every throw that I did,” Daurua said.

“This Best Player award, I want to dedicate this Best Player award to my dad and my mom for supporting me throughout my journey, which was a hard season.”

For the Kadavu-born forward, the individual award was made even more special by the journey behind it and the sacrifices made by his parents throughout the season.

Daurua’s performance was also symbolic of Grammar’s triumph, with the school’s forwards dominating the collisions and providing the foundation for a six-tries-to-three victory.

Grammar captain Waisale Bolakoro credited their historic triumph to the guidance and influence of coach Epeli Osbourne, who was himself a Deans winner during his playing days.

Bolakoro said Osbourne’s experience and knowledge of what it takes to win the Deans title inspired the team throughout their campaign.

“He was a Deans winner himself, so he knew what it took to get us here,” Bolakoro said.

“He believed in us, and we believed in him. This win is for our school, our parents, our old scholars and everyone who supported us.”

item.title: Ba Sangam claims U17 title
item.description: Ba Sangam College has been crowned the U17 champion of the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship after a determined campaign in Labasa. The side, coached by Prashneil Kumar, completed its title-winning run after overcoming Labasa Muslim College 4-1 in a penalty shootout.
item.content:encoded:
Ba Sangam College has been crowned the U17 champion of the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship after a determined campaign in Labasa.

The side, coached by Prashneil Kumar, completed its title-winning run after overcoming Labasa Muslim College 4-1 in a penalty shootout.

Kumar said the team’s success was built on hard work, belief and the commitment shown by his players throughout the tournament.

“I always have the belief in my players. I knew my players would deliver,” Kumar said.

He said the players had remained committed despite a demanding schedule, with some having to play several matches in a day.

“Nothing replaces hard work, and our boys have really worked hard,” he said.

Kumar said he was proud of the players for continuing to give their best despite the physical demands of the competition.

“I am so proud of the boys. They have been playing three games in a day. Sometimes they have to play back-to-back four games,” he said.

The coach also acknowledged the support from the players’ families, teachers and staff, dedicating the team’s success to those who had supported them from home.

The U17 triumph adds another highlight to Ba Sangam College’s campaign at the championship, with the players’ hard work rewarded with the national title.

item.title: Lelean break northern hearts
item.description: LELEAN Memorial School broke northern hearts but created their own piece of glory after edging Navatu Secondary School 15-14 in a pulsating Vodafone Super Deans under-19 final at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva yesterday. For Navatu, it was a cruel end to a remarkable campaign.
item.content:encoded:
LELEAN Memorial School broke northern hearts but created their own piece of glory after edging Navatu Secondary School 15-14 in a pulsating Vodafone Super Deans under-19 final at the HFC Bank National Stadium in Suva yesterday.

For Navatu, it was a cruel end to a remarkable campaign.

The northern champions had arrived at the final with history within reach as the first school from the North to contest a Vodafone Super Deans final, but a missed penalty with the final act of the match denied them a fairytale finish.

Navatu came out firing, dominating territory and pinning Lelean deep inside their own red zone for much of the opening half.

Their exceptional handling, willingness to shift the ball and expansive running game troubled the Davuilevu side as they crossed for two converted tries to establish a 14-0 lead.

They stayed composed, tightened their discipline and gradually worked their way back into the contest, scoring a try and adding a penalty to cut the deficit to 14-8 at halftime.

The Davuilevu side lifted the tempo and eventually crossed for a converted try to take a 15-14 lead for the first time in the match.

From there, their well-organised defence and improved discipline proved decisive as they kept the desperate Navatu attack at bay and forced their northern opponents into costly errors and penalties.

Navatu were handed one final opportunity when awarded a penalty in the dying moments, but the kick failed to find its target, sparking wild celebrations among the Lelean players and supporters.

Lelean head coach Peni Vakatawakoula said his side had prepared for the physical and fast-paced challenge Navatu brought.

“The boys stuck to the game plan and it paid off in the end,” he said.

“We had anticipated a tough match against Navatu and they did just that, but the message to the boys was to trust our processes. They did just that and the result speaks for itself.”

For Navatu captain and number eight Vilimone Kanawabu, the defeat was difficult to accept.

“That was a really close game that we should have won. The pressure and our mistakes cost us the match,” he said.

“I still can’t believe we let that match slip.”

Yet, despite the heartbreak, Kanawabu urged northern schools not to lose belief.

“For so long we have doubted ourselves in the North, but my message to all the players and teams back in the North is that anything is possible. The secret is faith and hard work.”

For Vakatawakoula, the victory belonged to more than just the 23 players who took the field.

He dedicated the title to the school, its old scholars, loyal supporters and the players’ families, whom he described as the pillars behind the team’s journey throughout the season.

item.title: Maroons edge Rewa in Round 4
item.description: KHELVIN Civil Engineering Lautoka Maroons secured their first win of the Skipper Cup season with a 28-23 victory over FMF Rewa Senior Men’s in Round Four at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday. Head coach Kiniviliame Bavadra praised his players for showing resilience and intensity on the field.
item.content:encoded:
KHELVIN Civil Engineering Lautoka Maroons secured their first win of the Skipper Cup season with a 28-23 victory over FMF Rewa Senior Men’s in Round Four at Churchill Park in Lautoka yesterday.

Head coach Kiniviliame Bavadra praised his players for showing resilience and intensity on the field.

After suffering defeats in their opening three matches, the Maroons finally broke through against Rewa, holding their nerve despite playing with only 12 men on the field.

Bavadra described the victory as a major boost for his side and a sign that the team is prepared to fight until the final whistle.

“I would say it’s a big green light for us in terms of staying in the fight and fighting until the end of the game,” Bavadra said.

However, the coach acknowledged that discipline remains an area the Maroons must improve after three yellow cards were issued to his players in the second half.

Bavadra said the problem was not simply discipline but also the players’ mindset and decision-making in crucial areas of the game.

“It can’t be just discipline alone but mindset in terms of how we want to engage in certain areas where we are already ;acking,” he said.

He said the team had discussed the breakdown during the halftime break and attempted to add numbers, but some players were penalised for cynical play.

“It’s really unnecessary and it goes back to how we prepare ourselves,” Bavadra said.

Following three consecutive losses, Bavadra said the message to his players was simple — continue grinding and find a way to win.

“The message is just to grind and get the win in a way that we haven’t showed or displayed in the previous three games,” he said.

The coach was particularly pleased with the intensity his players maintained throughout the match.

What I’m happy with was the intensity. We stayed in the game,” he said.

“We’ve been missing those for the first three games and I’m happy with the way they ended the match to get the win 28-23 against Rewa.”

We dedicated the win to the vanua, players families, supporters and fans of the Lautoka Maroons.

item.title: Tavua College shine
item.description: Western schools finished the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship on top, claiming four titles across the major grades. The final piece of the Western success came when Tavua College defeated Labasa College 2-0 in the U19 final, the last match of the championship.
item.content:encoded:
Western schools finished the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship on top, claiming four titles across the major grades.

The final piece of the Western success came when Tavua College defeated Labasa College 2-0 in the U19 final, the last match of the championship.

Tavua’s victory followed title-winning performances from other Western schools across the tournament.

Lautoka Central College won the U15 title after edging AD Patel College 1-0, while Ba Sangam College secured the U17 crown with a 4-1 victory over Labasa Muslim College.

Tavua also claimed the open-grade girls title, adding to its successful campaign.

The results highlighted the strength and depth of school football in the Western Division, with schools producing champions across the age groups and the open-grade girls competition.

The U19 final provided a fitting finish to the championship, with Tavua College completing the Western schools’ strong showing with a two-goal victory over Labasa College.

The four titles capped an impressive tournament for Western schools, which returned home with the major honours across the championship’s key grades.
